title: Prospective isolation of neural stem and progenitor cells from the developing human brain
protocol: Reconstitute fetal human brain tissue using a combination of mechanical and enzymatic digestion to dissociate it into a single-cell suspension.
Deplete red blood cells from the dissociated tissue using a density gradient method.
Perform dissection of specific brain regions if needed, although this step is optional.
Optimize the protocol for gestational week 16–20 cortical tissue but apply it to any brain region as necessary.
Store fetal human brain tissue overnight on ice without significant impact on viability or cell type makeup.
Transfer tissue to a 50 mL tube.
Spin down the sample at 300 × g for 3 min.
Remove supernatant.
Note the packed volume of the tissue.
Transfer the tissue into a sterile petri dish with 5 mL cold Mincing Buffer.
Chop the sample with sterile razor blades, aiming for 1–2 mm sized chunks.
Transfer the minced sample into 50 mL tubes, washing the petri dish with additional Mincing Buffer as needed.
Spin down the minced tissue at 300 × g for 3 min.
Remove supernatant.
Resuspend the minced tissue in pre-warmed Liberase Enzyme Solution, 30 mL per tube.
Shake the tubes on a thermomixer at 37°C and 750 RPM for 30 min.
Spin down the cell suspension at 300 × g for 3 min.
Remove 20 mL supernatant per tube, leaving behind 10 mL volume for trituration.
Triturate the cell suspension with progressively smaller-aperture pipettes.
Pipette the cell suspension up and down with a 10 mL serological pipette until it goes through smoothly (typically 10–15 strokes).
If cell suspension has large chunks, shake in Liberase Enzyme Solution for an additional 15 minutes.
Attach a P1000 pipette tip (no filter) to the end of a 10 mL serological pipette and cut off approximately 5 mm from the end with a sterile razor blade.
Pipette cell suspension up and down until it passes through smoothly, typically 10-15 strokes.
Attach a P1000 pipette tip (no filter) to the end of a 10 mL serological pipette without cutting off the tip.
Pipette cell suspension up and down until it passes through smoothly, typically 10-15 strokes.
Fill tube with Wash Buffer.
Spin down cell suspension at 300 x g for 3 minutes.
Remove supernatant.
Resuspend cell pellet in Accutase Enzyme Solution, using 25 mL per tube.
Shake tubes on a Thermomixer at 25°C and 750 RPM for 30 minutes.
Add DNase to the enzyme solution before shaking.
Spin down cell suspension at 300 x g for 3 minutes.
Remove supernatant.
Wash cells with 10 mL Wash Buffer.
Spin down cell suspension at 300 x g for 3 minutes.
Remove supernatant.
Resuspend cell pellet in 9 mL Wash Buffer per tube.
Prepare one FACS tube per 3 mL of cell suspension.
Add 1 mL Ficoll to each tube.
Gently layer 3 mL cell suspension on top of Ficoll for each tube.
Spin the tubes at 400 × g for 30 min at 25°C with acceleration set to 4 out of 10 and brakes turned off.
Carefully pipette the upper layer and buffy coat from the interface of the two layers after centrifugation.
Transfer the upper layer and buffy coat into a new 50 mL tube.
Stain the cell suspension with fluorescently-labeled antibodies.
Set aside a small number of cells for an unstained control (1% of total cells).
Stain the cell suspension by resuspending it in Primary Staining Solution.
Incubate the cells on ice for 20 minutes.
Protect from light during incubation.
Wash the cells with 2 mL Wash Buffer.
Spin down at 300 × g for 3 minutes.
Remove supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in Secondary Staining Solution.
Incubate the cells on ice for 20 minutes.
Protect from light during incubation.
Wash the cells with 2 mL Wash Buffer.
Spin down at 300 × g for 3 minutes.
Remove supernatant.
Perform this step twice prior to analysis.
Add propidium iodide to the cells immediately prior to analysis.
Prepare compensation controls.
Prepare one FACS tube for each fluorophore on the panel, as well as a negative control.
In the unstained control tube, add one drop of negative control compensation particles.
In each stained tube, add one drop each of Anti-Rat/Anti-Hamster Ig, κ compensation particles and Anti-Mouse Ig, κ compensation particles.
Add 1 μL of any antibody conjugated to the corresponding fluorophore to each stained tube.
Add 300 μL Wash Buffer to each tube.
Run Cytometer Setup and Tracking (CST) to set voltages.
Select all fluorophores used in the staining panel, in addition to PI, forward scatter, and side scatter.
Set forward and side scatter on a linear scale and all other channels on a log scale.
Run compensation controls and apply the compensation matrix.
Set the Drop Delay using Auto Delay.
Aim each of the four streams to ensure they hit the bottom of the collection tube.
Plot FSC-A against SSC-A.
Gate for Cells.
From Cells, plot FSC-H against FSC-W.
Gate for Singlets (FSC).
From Singlets (FSC), plot SSC-H against SSC-W.
Gate for Singlets (SSC).
From Singlets (SSC), plot Lineage-PE against PI.
Gate for Live Lineage−.
From Live Lineage−, plot CD24-APC against THY1-FITC.
Gate for CD24−THY1−/lo, enriched for radial glia and astrocytes.
Gate for CD24+THY1−/lo, enriched for neuron precursors.
Gate for THY1hi, enriched for oligodendrocyte lineages.
From CD24−THY1−/lo, plot CXCR4-APC/Cy7 against EGFR-PE/Cy7.
Gate for EGFR+CXCR4−, enriched for ventricular radial glia (vRG).
Gate for EGFR−CXCR4−, enriched for outer radial glia (oRG).
Gate for EGFR+CXCR4+, enriched for astrocytes (AC).
From THY1hi, plot PDGFRA-BUV395 against EGFR-PE/Cy7.
Plot CXCR4-APC/Cy7 against EGFR-PE/Cy7 from CD24+THY1−/lo cells.
Gate for EGFR+CXCR4−, enriched for early excitatory neurons (ExN).
Sort cells for EGFR+CXCR4− population.
Load collection tubes with 0.5 mL Wash Buffer and vortex prior to loading.
Sort cells on four-way purity until the desired number of cells is obtained.
Prepare 96 well plates filled with 100 μL Fetal Growth Media for neurosphere initiation assay.
Add antibiotic/antimycotic to the media for freshly isolated cells.
Sort cells into wells according to desired cell numbers.
Replace half the volume of each well with fresh Fetal Growth Media weekly.
Coat 96 well plates with polyornithine and laminin.
Add 50 μL polyornithine solution (20 μg/mL) to each well.
Incubate at 37°C for at least 1 h.
Aspirate the polyornithine solution.
Add 50 μL laminin solution (50 μg/mL) to each well.
Incubate at 37°C for at least 1 h.
Aspirate the laminin solution.
Spin down the sorted cells at 300 × g for 3 min.
Resuspend in Differentiation Media at a concentration of 5×10^4 cells/mL.
Add 100 μL of the cell suspension per well, which gives 5×10^3 cells per well.
After 5 days, fix the cells by adding 100 μL 4% PFA on top of the media.
Fix for 15 min at 4°C.
Remove the PFA and wash three times with 200 μL PBS.
Perform immunofluorescent staining for lineage markers of interest.
Image stained cells on a fluorescent microscope.
Spin down sorted cells at 300 × g for 3 minutes.
Resuspend cells in Fast Green dye at a concentration of 105 cells/μL.
Anesthetize neonatal NSG pups by wrapping them in tissue and covering with ice for 2 minutes.
Place anesthetized pup on a stereotaxic device fitted with a mouse neonate adaptor.
Secure the pup’s head using the adaptor.
Keep the platform of the stereotaxic device cold to maintain anesthesia.
Load cell suspension into a Hamilton syringe with a 33-gauge needle.
Load the syringe onto a microsyringe pump controller.
Make a burr hole at the injection site using a 30-gauge needle.
Position the syringe for lateral ventricles with coordinates (A, L, V) = (0.8, ±1.5, 2.0) mm from midline and surface of brain, respectively.
Inject cells at a rate of 1 μL/min, injecting 1 μL per side.
Warm the pup on a 37°C heating pad or in your palm until movement is observed.
Reintroduce the pup to its mother.
Wait between 3–6 months for the mouse to mature.
Sacrifice mouse.
Anesthetize the mouse using isoflurane.
Open the thoracic cavity to expose the heart.
Cut the right atrium.
Inject 20 mL PBS with 5 mM EDTA into the left ventricle to perfuse the mouse.
Decapitate the mouse and dissect out the brain.
Fix brains in 4% PFA for histology or dissociate to recover engrafted human cells.
